subject: Physics
title: Simple Harmonic Motion
learningOutcomes: Define oscillation, displacement, amplitude, time period, frequency and angular frequency, and distinguish free, forced and damped oscillations.
Show that a mass on a spring and a simple pendulum (small angles) execute SHM, and use T = 2π√(m/k) and T = 2π√(l/g).
Relate SHM to uniform circular motion and use x = x₀ cos(ωt + φ), v = ω√(x₀² − x²) and a = −ω²x, including phase and phase difference.
Explain how kinetic and potential energy change in SHM while the total energy ½kx₀² stays constant.
Describe light, critical and heavy damping and resonance, with applications such as radio tuning, microwave ovens, MRI, bridges and the Rubens tube.

sections.heading: Oscillations & Their Terms
sections.body: A body that moves to and fro about a mean position executes oscillatory (vibratory) motion; one complete round trip is one oscillation. Displacement is the distance from the mean position at any instant, amplitude is the maximum displacement, the time period T is the time for one oscillation and the frequency f = 1/T is the number of oscillations per second (hertz). Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π/T is measured in rad s⁻¹.

sections.heading: Simple Harmonic Motion & Hooke's Law
sections.body: SHM is the motion in which the acceleration is proportional to the displacement and always directed towards the mean position: a = −ω²x. A spring obeys Hooke's law, F = −kx, where k (N m⁻¹) is the spring constant and the negative sign means the restoring force opposes the displacement. A mass m on the spring has ω = √(k/m) and T = 2π√(m/k) — independent of the amplitude.

sections.heading: Simple Pendulum
sections.body: A simple pendulum is a small heavy bob on a light, inextensible string of length l. The tension cancels the component mg cos θ of the weight and the component mg sin θ is the restoring force. For small angles (less than about 10°) sin θ ≈ θ, giving a = −(g/l)x and T = 2π√(l/g). The time period depends on l and g but not on the mass of the bob.

sections.heading: SHM & Circular Motion, Phase, Graphs
sections.body: The projection of a body moving uniformly in a circle of radius x₀ on a diameter executes SHM. This gives x = x₀ cos ωt, v = ω√(x₀² − x²) and a = −ω²x, with v_max = ωx₀ at the mean position and a_max = ω²x₀ at the extremes. The angle ωt is the phase; x = x₀ cos(ωt + φ) includes an initial phase φ. Velocity leads displacement by π/2 and acceleration is opposite (π) to displacement.

sections.heading: Energy in SHM
sections.body: The energy of a mass-spring system keeps changing between kinetic and potential forms while the total stays constant: P.E = ½kx², K.E = ½k(x₀² − x²) and T.E = ½kx₀². At the mean position all the energy is kinetic; at the extreme positions all of it is potential. The total energy is proportional to the square of the amplitude.

sections.heading: Free, Forced & Damped Oscillations; Resonance
sections.body: Free oscillations occur under a restoring force alone; forced oscillations are driven by an external periodic force at a driven frequency. Damping removes energy as heat: light damping (a swing slowly coming to rest), heavy damping (a spring in thick liquid) and critical damping (car shock absorbers, returning to equilibrium in the shortest time). Resonance occurs when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency, giving maximum amplitude — useful in radio tuning, microwave ovens, MRI and the guitar box, but dangerous for bridges (Tacoma Narrows) and airplane wings.

definitions.definition: One complete round trip of a body about its mean position.
The distance of a vibrating body from the equilibrium position at any instant.
The maximum displacement of a vibrating body from its mean position.
The time taken to complete one oscillation.
The number of oscillations completed per unit time; its SI unit is the hertz.
The angular displacement per unit time, ω = 2πf, in rad s⁻¹.
Oscillatory motion in which the acceleration is proportional to the displacement and directed towards the mean position.
The force that always acts towards the equilibrium position of an oscillating body.
The restoring force of a spring is proportional to its displacement: F = −kx.
The angle ωt that specifies the displacement and direction of motion of a point in SHM.
Oscillation under a restoring force with no external force acting on the body.
Oscillation of a body driven by an external periodic force at a driven frequency.
The effect of resistive forces that remove energy from a vibrating object, so its amplitude decreases.
The condition in which the amplitude of an oscillator is maximum because the driving frequency equals its natural frequency.

examTips: Memorise T = 2π√(m/k) and T = 2π√(l/g) — and which quantities do not appear (amplitude, and the bob's mass for a pendulum).
v is maximum (ωx₀) and a is zero at the mean position; v is zero and a is maximum (ω²x₀) at the extreme positions.
K.E + P.E = ½kx₀² at every instant; at x = x₀/2 the oscillator holds 25% potential and 75% kinetic energy.
Convert units before substituting: cm → m, and use g = 9.8 m/s² unless the question gives another value.
Light, critical and heavy damping: compare how fast the amplitude falls and whether the body oscillates before stopping.
For resonance questions always state: driving frequency = natural frequency → maximum amplitude → maximum energy transfer.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The motion of a body that moves to and fro about its mean position is called:
practiceQuestions.explanation: A to-and-fro motion about a mean position is oscillatory (vibratory) motion.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The maximum displacement of a vibrating body from its mean position is called its:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The SI unit of frequency is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz): one oscillation per second.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In F = −kx the negative sign shows that the restoring force:
practiceQuestions.explanation: The restoring force acts opposite to the displacement, towards the equilibrium position.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In SHM the acceleration is directly proportional to the displacement and is always directed:
practiceQuestions.explanation: a = −ω²x: proportional to x and directed towards the mean position.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A heavier mass is hung on the same spring. Its time period will:
A 0.5 kg mass is attached to a spring of constant 50 N/m. Its time period is:
A simple pendulum of length 1 m on Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²) has a time period of about:
At the mean position of a mass-spring system the total energy is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: At x = 0 the spring is unstretched, so P.E = 0 and all the energy is kinetic.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A particle in SHM has amplitude 0.2 m and angular frequency 5 rad/s. Its maximum speed is:
Damping decreases the amplitude of an oscillator with time.
practiceQuestions.explanation: True — resistive forces remove energy from the oscillator, so the amplitude falls.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The time period of a simple pendulum depends on the mass of its bob.
practiceQuestions.explanation: False — T = 2π√(l/g) does not contain the mass.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Resonance occurs when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency of the oscillator.
practiceQuestions.explanation: True — at resonance the amplitude of vibration is maximum.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The time taken to complete one oscillation is called the _____.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The time period T is the time for one complete oscillation; f = 1/T.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The angle ωt that gives the displacement and direction of a point in SHM is called the _____ of the motion.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The angle ωt is the phase of the motion.

sequencingActivity.prompt: Arrange the steps in deriving the time period of a mass-spring system:

items: Compare with a = −ω²x of SHM to get ω² = k/m
correctOrder: Compare with a = −ω²x of SHM to get ω² = k/m

sequencingActivity.explanation: Hooke's law → Newton's second law → compare with SHM → T = 2π√(m/k).

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A 2 kg mass on a spring of constant 200 N/m oscillates with amplitude 0.1 m. What is its maximum speed?
The same simple pendulum is taken from Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²) to the Moon (g = 1.6 m/s²). Its time period becomes about:
The mass on a spring is made four times as large and the amplitude is doubled. The new time period is:
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: T ∝ √m gives a factor of 2; the time period does not depend on amplitude.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: At a displacement x = x₀/2, what percentage of the total energy of a SHM oscillator is kinetic?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: P.E/T.E = (x/x₀)² = 1/4, so K.E = 1 − 1/4 = 75% of the total energy.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A 0.25 m simple pendulum (g = 9.8 m/s²) is pushed periodically. At which driving frequency does it resonate?
